title: ‘Zombie’ electricity projects in Britain face axe to ease quicker grid connections — The Guardian
text:
Title: ‘Zombie’ electricity projects in Britain face axe to ease quicker grid connections — The Guardian

Separately, Monday marks 25 years of offshore wind power generation in the UK since the first turbines were erected at Blyth off the coast of Northumberland. Britain’s 47 operational offshore windfarms now supply nearly a fifth (17%) of its electricity generation – making it the second-biggest power source after gas – with the sector employing about 40,000 people, according to an analysis released on Monday by green group Ember. • This article was amended on 8 December 2025. An earlier version said it was 25 years since the UK’s first wind turbines were erected; in fact, it is 25 years since the UK’s first offshore windfarm was installed.
